segments.s107: What is CGPA, and how is it different from GPA and SGPA?
segments.s108: CGPA stands for Cumulative Grade Point Average. It is one number that sums up how you have performed across every semester you have completed so far. Universities print it on your transcript, employers ask for it on job applications, and scholarship committees use it to shortlist students. When someone says "my CGPA is 3.4", they mean their average for the whole degree up to now, not just the last semester.
segments.s109: The three terms sound alike, so here is the simple difference:
segments.s115: Your average for one semester (in some countries, for a year or the whole degree)
segments.s118: Your average for one semester. This is the name most Indian universities use, and it means the same as a semester GPA.
segments.s121: Your average across all the semesters you have completed
segments.s122: In short, SGPA and semester GPA describe one semester, while CGPA describes your whole journey. In the USA, "GPA" on its own often means the cumulative figure, which is why the words get mixed up. If a form asks about your degree as a whole, it almost always wants the cumulative number.
segments.s123: All three are weighted by credit hours. A 4-credit course affects your average more than a 1-credit lab, because it stands for more teaching time and more work.
segments.s124: How to calculate CGPA step by step
segments.s125: You don't need any special maths, just your grades and the credit hours of each course. This is the method most universities use:
segments.s126: Turn each grade into grade points. Use your university's grade point table (see the tables below). On the 4.0 scale, an A is usually 4.00 and a B+ is 3.33.
segments.s127: Multiply grade points by credit hours. This gives the "quality points" for each course. A 3-credit course with an A earns 3 × 4.00 = 12 quality points.
segments.s128: Work out the semester GPA. Add up the quality points for the semester and divide by the total credit hours. That is your semester GPA, or SGPA.
segments.s129: Combine your semesters. Multiply each semester's GPA by that semester's credit hours, add the results, and divide by the total credit hours of all semesters. The answer is your CGPA.
segments.s130: CGPA = Σ (semester GPA × semester credits) ÷ Σ (semester credits)

segments.s187: A CGPA can feel stuck, but it moves more than you might think, especially early in your degree. These habits make a real difference:
segments.s188: Focus on high-credit courses. A good grade in a 4-credit course lifts your CGPA more than the same grade in a 1-credit course, so plan your study time around that.
segments.s189: Don't ignore internal marks. Quizzes, assignments, labs and attendance often make up a big part of the final grade, and they are the easiest marks to secure.
segments.s190: Study a little every day. Reviewing your notes for 30 minutes after class works better than an all-night session before the exam, and you remember more.
segments.s191: Solve past papers. They show you the question style, the topics that come up most and how marks are awarded.
segments.s192: Ask for help early. Visit your teacher's office hours or ask a classmate in the week you get confused, not the week before finals.
segments.s193: Retake courses wisely. If your university replaces the old grade when you repeat a course, retaking a D or F can be one of the fastest ways to raise your CGPA.
segments.s194: Set a clear target. Use the Target tab to see exactly what GPA you need. "I need a 3.4 this semester" is much easier to act on than "I need to do better".
segments.s195: Look after yourself. Sleep, food and short breaks aren't wasted time. Tired students make careless mistakes in exams.
segments.s196: As your total credits grow, each new semester has a smaller effect on your CGPA. That means improving early is much easier than improving in your final year, so the best time to start is this semester.
segments.s198: Is CGPA the same as GPA?
segments.s199: Not exactly. GPA usually means your average for one semester, while CGPA is your average across all the semesters you have completed. In the USA, though, "GPA" on a transcript often means the cumulative figure. If a form asks for your GPA for the whole degree, give your CGPA.
segments.s200: How do I calculate CGPA from SGPA?
segments.s201: Multiply each semester's SGPA by that semester's credits, add the results, and divide by your total credits. If every semester has exactly the same number of credits, a simple average of your SGPAs gives the same answer.
segments.s202: Can I just average my semester GPAs?
segments.s203: Only when every semester has the same credit hours. Otherwise you need a credit-weighted average, because heavier semesters count for more. The CGPA tab of this calculator does this for you.
segments.s204: How do I convert CGPA to percentage?
segments.s205: On the 4.0 scale, divide your CGPA by 4 and multiply by 100. On the 10-point scale, the common method is CGPA × 9.5. Always check whether your university has its own official formula, because that is the one employers and admissions offices will use.
segments.s206: Why do we multiply by 9.5 for a 10-point CGPA?
segments.s207: CBSE introduced the 9.5 factor after comparing grade points with the marks students actually scored in past exams. Many Indian universities have adopted it, but not all of them, so check your university's rule.
segments.s209: On the 4.0 scale, 3.5 or above is generally seen as excellent and 3.0 or above as good. On the 10-point scale, 8.0 or above is strong and 7.0 or above is good. Cut-offs for jobs, scholarships and higher studies vary, so always check the exact requirement.
segments.s210: Can I raise my CGPA from 2.5 to 3.0?
segments.s211: Usually yes, if you have enough credits left. For example, with a 2.50 CGPA after 60 credits and 70 credits still to go, you need an average of about 3.43 in your remaining semesters. The Target tab of this calculator works this out for your own numbers.
segments.s212: Do failed or repeated courses count in CGPA?
segments.s213: It depends on your university. Many count an F as zero grade points until you pass the course. Some replace the old grade when you repeat a course, while others keep both grades in the average. Check your university's repeat policy.
segments.s214: How many decimal places should I write for my CGPA?
segments.s215: Most universities show CGPA to two decimal places, for example 3.37. On forms and CVs, write it exactly as it appears on your official transcript, and don't round it up yourself.

You get one grade for all 4 credits, so enter it in the calculator as one 4-credit subject.

segments.s261: Minimum CGPA and academic deficiency at NUST
segments.s262: To graduate you need a minimum CGPA of 2.00, or 2.50 for BBA, BS Economics, BS Public Administration, BS Mass Communication, BS Accounting & Finance and BS Psychology.
segments.s263: BE and BS students also need at least a C in their final-year (design) project, where applicable.
segments.s264: You are academically deficient if you get an F or XF in any course, a semester GPA below 2.00, a CGPA below 2.00, an I (incomplete) grade, or less than a C in your final-year project.
segments.s265: If your CGPA has dropped below 2.00, the Target tab shows the GPA you need in your remaining semesters to get back above it.
segments.s266: Repeating a course to improve your CGPA
segments.s267: When you repeat a course, your transcript shows both the old and the new grade, but only the better grade is used to compute your CGPA. Repeating needs permission from your HoD, and grades earned by repeating don't count towards top academic honours and awards, except the Rector's Gold Medal. If you fail a course again after repeating it, it still counts as one F.
segments.s268: Calculator tip: for a repeated course, enter only the better grade.
segments.s270: The NUST Undergraduate Student Handbook does not include an official formula for converting CGPA into a percentage. When a percentage is needed, many people use (CGPA ÷ 4) × 100, so 3.40 becomes 85%. Employers and universities sometimes use their own rules, so check what the organisation you're applying to accepts. The Percentage tab uses this simple method.
segments.s272: Does NUST use relative or absolute grading?
segments.s273: NUST uses relative grading on a 4.00 scale, so your grade depends on your performance compared with your class rather than on a fixed percentage. That is why there is no fixed marks-to-grade table for NUST.
segments.s274: What are the grade points for each grade at NUST?
segments.s275: A is 4.00, B+ is 3.50, B is 3.00, C+ is 2.50, C is 2.00, D+ is 1.50 and D is 1.00. F and XF (F because of a shortage of attendance) are 0.00. D+ and D are used for undergraduate students only.
segments.s276: Is there an A+ or A- grade at NUST?
segments.s277: No. A (4.00) is the highest grade and there are no minus grades. B+ and C+ sit half a point above B and C.
segments.s278: What CGPA do I need to graduate from NUST?
segments.s279: A minimum CGPA of 2.00, or 2.50 for BBA, BS Economics, BS Public Administration, BS Mass Communication, BS Accounting & Finance and BS Psychology. BE and BS students also need at least a C in their final-year project where applicable.
segments.s280: If I repeat a course at NUST, which grade counts?
segments.s281: Your transcript shows both grades, but only the better grade is used in your CGPA. Grades earned by repeating do not count towards top academic awards, except the Rector’s Gold Medal.
segments.s282: How do I convert my NUST CGPA to a percentage?
segments.s283: The NUST undergraduate handbook does not give an official formula. The common method is (CGPA ÷ 4) × 100, so 3.40 becomes 85%, but check what the employer or university you are applying to accepts.
segments.s284: How do I enter a course that has a lab?
segments.s285: Enter it as one subject with its total credit hours, for example 4 for a 3+1 course. NUST combines the theory and lab marks into one grade for the whole course.

segments.s325: Why does COMSATS give a range of grade points for each grade?
segments.s326: Since Fall 2021, COMSATS follows the HEC grading criteria, where each letter grade covers a range of grade points. Your exact points depend on your marks, so two students with an A- can have different grade points.
segments.s327: How do I convert my COMSATS CGPA to a percentage?
segments.s328: Find the band your CGPA falls in and take the lowest percentage of that band. For example, 3.40 is in the A- band (3.34 to 3.66), so it equals 80%. The Percentage tab does this for you.
segments.s329: What percentage is a 3.00 CGPA at COMSATS?
segments.s330: It is 71%. This exact example is given in the COMSATS notification: a 3.00 CGPA falls in the B band (2.67 to 3.00), whose lowest percentage is 71%.
segments.s331: Can I use CGPA × 25 or (CGPA ÷ 4) × 100 for COMSATS?
segments.s332: Not for students admitted from Fall 2021. Those formulas usually give a higher number than the official COMSATS rule, which uses the lowest percentage of the band your CGPA falls in.

segments.s389: Why do some websites say to subtract 0.75 from VTU CGPA?

segments.s391: What CGPA do I need for First Class with Distinction in VTU?

segments.s393: What are the passing marks in the VTU 2022 scheme?

segments.s395: Is VTU grading relative or absolute?

segments.s397: How is CGPA calculated from SGPA in VTU?

segments.s610: Most degrees are classified on the 3rd and 4th (Honours) years; years 1 and 2 don’t count.

segments.s612: A mark within 2 points below a boundary (e.g. 68.00–69.99) is borderline and must be considered.
segments.s614: The University of Edinburgh classifies most undergraduate Honours degrees on the average mark of all courses taken in the third and fourth years, the Honours years, weighted by each course's credits. Every 10 credits count the same, so a 40-credit dissertation weighs four times as much as a 10-credit course. The first two years don't count towards your class, so you can take a broad range of courses there without it affecting your degree result.
segments.s615: There are exceptions. BSc Honours degrees in the School of Biological Sciences, the Deanery of Biomedical Sciences and Chemistry weight Senior to Junior Honours 2:1. Integrated Masters degrees use their three Honours years weighted 20, 40 and 40. For degrees with optional study abroad in third year, only the final year counts.
segments.s629: Each final course mark is rounded to a whole number before it is released: 59.50 becomes 60 and 59.49 becomes 59. Those rounded course marks are used to work out your overall mean, and the overall mean itself is not rounded. So a mean of 69.90 is not a First on its own.
segments.s630: However, the regulations define borderline marks as those from two percentage points below a class boundary up to the boundary, for example 68.00% to 69.99% for a First or 58.00% to 59.99% for a 2:1. The Board of Examiners must consider every borderline student, using factors it has published in advance, such as better performance in higher-level courses.
segments.s639: Edinburgh doesn't use a GPA. If you apply abroad, send your transcript with your marks and class; the receiving university or employer will convert them with its own rules.
segments.s641: Which years count towards an Edinburgh Honours degree?
segments.s642: For most degrees, the third and fourth years (the Honours years). Courses are weighted by credits. Some programmes differ, for example Integrated Masters weight their three Honours years 20, 40 and 40.
segments.s643: What mark is a First at Edinburgh?
segments.s644: An overall mean of 70 or more. Grades A1 (90–100), A2 (80–89) and A3 (70–79) are all in the First Class band.
segments.s645: Does Edinburgh round the final average?
segments.s646: No. Course marks are rounded to whole numbers before they are released, but the overall mean used for your class is not rounded.
segments.s647: What is a borderline mark at Edinburgh?
segments.s648: A mark from two percentage points below a class boundary up to the boundary, such as 68.00% to 69.99% for a First. The Board of Examiners must consider these cases.
segments.s649: What does a B grade mean at Edinburgh?
segments.s650: A B is a mark of 60–69, described as very good, and is in the Upper Second (2:1) band.
segments.s652: No. Edinburgh uses marks out of 100 and Honours classes. A university or employer abroad will convert your transcript with its own rules.

segments.s661: Choose the letter grade on your record for each course. Grade points come from the Harvard FAS grade point average rules.
segments.s663: Harvard FAS uses a 4.0 scale with plus and minus grades: A = 4.00, A- = 3.67, B+ = 3.33.
segments.s664: There is no A+. The failing grade is E, worth 0, and UNS, ABS and EXLD also count as 0.
segments.s665: Grades from other Harvard schools or MIT only enter your GPA if they are failing grades.
segments.s667: The Faculty of Arts and Sciences (FAS), which runs Harvard College, turns every letter grade into points on a 4-point scale. Your grade point average is the average of the grades you received in letter-graded FAS courses taken for degree credit. Courses graded Satisfactory (SAT) don't add points, but an Unsatisfactory (UNS) counts as 0.
segments.s668: Harvard instructors set grades for their own courses, so there is no university-wide table that turns a percentage into a letter. That's why this calculator asks for the letter grade on your record.
segments.s671: Grades from courses at other Harvard Faculties or at MIT are not used in your FAS grade point average unless they are failing grades. FAS has also announced that, from the 2027-28 academic year, an A may be given to at most 20 percent of the undergraduates in a course, plus four.
segments.s672: How to calculate your Harvard GPA: worked example
segments.s673: Most Harvard College courses carry the same weight (4 credits), so the GPA is a straight average of your grade points. If every course has the same credits, you can type 4 for each one.
segments.s679: Harvard does not convert GPAs into percentages, and American transcripts don't show one. If an application form outside the US insists on a percentage, the usual estimate is (GPA ÷ 4) × 100, so a 3.50 becomes 87.5%. Write "approximately" next to it and attach your transcript, because the university doesn't confirm this number.
segments.s681: What is an A- worth at Harvard?
segments.s682: An A- is worth 3.67 grade points. An A is 4.00, a B+ is 3.33, a B is 3.00 and a B- is 2.67.
segments.s684: No. In the Harvard FAS grade point average, A (4.00) is the highest grade. The failing grade is E, which is worth 0.
segments.s685: Do pass/fail (SAT/UNS) courses count in my Harvard GPA?
segments.s686: Satisfactory (SAT) courses do not add any points. An Unsatisfactory (UNS) counts as 0, like an E, so it lowers your GPA.
segments.s687: Do cross-registered courses at MIT count in my Harvard GPA?
segments.s688: Grades from other Harvard Faculties or from MIT are not used in your FAS grade point average, unless the grade is a failing grade.
segments.s689: How do I convert my Harvard GPA to a percentage?
segments.s690: Harvard does not publish a formula. If a form needs one, the usual estimate is (GPA ÷ 4) × 100, so 3.50 is about 87.5%. Mark it as an estimate.
segments.s691: What credits should I enter for each Harvard course?
segments.s692: Most Harvard College courses are 4 credits. When every course has the same credits, the GPA is simply the average of your grade points, so you can enter 4 for each course.

segments.s742: How grading works at Heidelberg University
segments.s743: Heidelberg University (Ruprecht-Karls-Universität Heidelberg) grades each piece of work from 1 (sehr gut) to 5 (nicht ausreichend), with intermediate steps of 0.3: 1.0, 1.3, 1.7, 2.0 and so on. The grades 0.7, 4.3, 4.7 and 5.3 are not used. A module made of several parts gets the average of its part grades, weighted by credit points (Leistungspunkte, LP), unless the module handbook says otherwise.

segments.s792: For a three-year honours degree (BA, BSc, BEng, LLB, BMus) the weighting is 0:2:3: Year 1 marks have a weight of 0, Year 2 marks 2 and Year 3 marks 3. segments.s811: King's doesn't calculate a GPA. If you apply abroad, send your transcript with your marks and class, and the receiving institution will convert it with its own rules.
segments.s813: Does first year count at King's College London?

segments.s815: What is the King's year weighting?
segments.s816: Three-year honours degrees use 0:2:3. Four-year degrees with a year abroad or in industry use 0:2:0:3, and integrated master’s degrees use 0:2:3:4.
segments.s817: Does King's round the final mark?

segments.s819: Is there a borderline zone at King's?

segments.s821: What mark do I need for a 2:1 at King's?
segments.s822: A classification score of 60 to 69 after rounding, which means 59.5 or more before rounding.
segments.s823: Does a semester abroad count at King's?

segments.s1073: How Oxford marks and classifies degrees
segments.s1074: Oxford examiners report each paper on a 0–100 scale called the University Standardised Mark (USM). The bands are the same across subjects: 70–100 is First Class, 60–69 Upper Second, 50–59 Lower Second, 40–49 Third, 30–39 Pass and 0–29 Fail.
segments.s1075: How the USMs are combined is set by each course's examination conventions, published every year by the department. Most courses use a weighted average, but the weights, the papers that count and any extra rules (for example a minimum number of papers in the First Class band) differ from course to course. Always check the conventions for your course and year.
segments.s1083: The Computer Science conventions give each paper a weight: 10 for each core course, 14 for each option and 42 for the Part B project, a total of 222. The weighted average is every USM multiplied by its weight, added up and divided by 222. That works out at about 18% for second-year exams and 82% for third-year exams. The average USM is then rounded to the nearest integer, with exact halves rounded up, so 69.5 becomes 70.
segments.s1084: To use the calculator, enter each paper's USM and its weight in the Average tab. If all your papers count the same, give every paper a weight of 1.
segments.s1094: Oxford doesn't calculate a GPA, and its transcripts show USMs and your class. There is no official Oxford formula for turning USMs into a 4.0 GPA.

segments.s1264: Universiti Malaya (UM) grades every course with a letter grade linked to a mark range and a grade point. Your semester GPA and your CGPA are the usual credit-weighted averages: multiply each course's grade point by its credit hours, add them up and divide by the total credit hours.
segments.s1265: Two things make UM's scale different from many others. First, both A+ and A are worth 4.0, so marks above 80 all give the full 4.0. Second, the lowest passing grade is C (50%). C-, D+ and D still carry grade points, but they are fail grades.

segments.s1498: How the CGPA to German grade conversion works
segments.s1499: German universities grade from 1.0 (the best) to 4.0 (the lowest pass). To compare a grade from another country, they use the modified Bavarian formula, which the Kultusministerkonferenz (KMK) recommends for grades earned abroad:
segments.s1500: Nd is your own grade, for example your CGPA or your percentage.
segments.s1501: Nmax is the best possible grade in your system, for example 4.0 on a 4.0 scale or 100 for percentages.
segments.s1502: Nmin is the lowest passing grade in your system, for example 2.0 on many 4.0 scales or 50 for percentages.
segments.s1503: The formula places your grade on a line between the best grade (which becomes 1.0) and the lowest pass (which becomes 4.0). The closer you are to the top of your scale, the closer your German grade is to 1.0.
segments.s1513: Worked example: CGPA 3.40 on a 4.0 scale
segments.s1514: Ali has a CGPA of 3.40 from a Pakistani university on the 4.0 scale, where the lowest passing CGPA is 2.0. So Nd = 3.40, Nmax = 4.0 and Nmin = 2.0:
segments.s1515: Ali's German grade is 1.90, or 1.9 with one decimal. That is in the gut (good) band.
segments.s1516: Percentages work the same way. With 75% where the pass mark is 50%: 1 + 3 × (100 − 75) ÷ (100 − 50) = 1 + 3 × 25 ÷ 50 = 2.50, which is also gut.
segments.s1517: Notice how much Nmin matters: if the lowest pass on Ali's scale were 1.0 instead of 2.0, the same 3.40 would give 1 + 3 × 0.6 ÷ 3.0 = 1.60. Always use the minimum passing grade your own university states.
segments.s1518: What is the Modified Bavarian Formula?
segments.s1519: It is the formula German universities use to turn a grade from another country into a German grade: German grade = 1 + 3 × (Nmax − Nd) ÷ (Nmax − Nmin). Nmax is the best grade in your system, Nmin the lowest passing grade and Nd your own grade. The Kultusministerkonferenz (KMK) recommends it for grades earned abroad.
segments.s1520: What is Nmin for my university?
segments.s1521: Nmin is the lowest grade that still counts as a pass in your grading system. Look for it in the grading key on your transcript or in your university's rules. Many Pakistani universities on the 4.0 scale use 2.0 (the minimum CGPA for a degree), and for percentages it is often 50% or 40%. German universities may also take it from the anabin database, so they can use a different value from yours.
segments.s1522: Is 1.0 the best grade in Germany?
segments.s1523: Yes. In the German system 1.0 is the best grade and 4.0 is the lowest pass. Anything worse than 4.0, such as 5.0, is a fail. So a smaller German grade is better, which is the opposite of a CGPA.
segments.s1525: Yes. uni-assist converts foreign grades with the modified Bavarian formula, for example in the VPD (preliminary review documentation), and keeps one decimal place without rounding, so 2.37 becomes 2.3. Each university still makes its own admission decision, and some convert grades themselves, so check the rules of every university you apply to.
segments.s1526: Can I convert percentage to German grade?
segments.s1527: Yes. Use 100 as Nmax and your system's pass mark as Nmin, for example 50% or 40%. With 75% and a pass mark of 50%, your German grade is 1 + 3 × (100 − 75) ÷ (100 − 50) = 2.50. Tap the Percentage button in the converter to fill these in.
